title: Strings
summary: Join text, drop values into it, and ask a string about itself.

steps.title: Joining text
body: `+` between strings glues them together. This is called **concatenation**.
Nothing adds spaces for you. `first + last` would print `AdaLovelace`.
If one side is a string, the other side is turned into text too:

steps.explain: `+` works left to right. Once a string is involved it joins text. In the last line `1 + 2` is still two numbers, so it becomes `3` before meeting the string.

steps.title: String interpolation
body: Lots of `+` signs get hard to read. Put a `$` before the opening quote and you can drop values straight into the text inside `{ }`.
Anything inside the braces is real code: a variable, a calculation, a method call.
A colon adds formatting. `{price:F2}` shows exactly two decimal places:

steps.prompt: Complete the line so it prints `Hello, Sam! You have 3 messages.`
steps.explain: Without the `$` the braces would be printed literally. Without the braces you would get the word `user`.

options: Nothing: it is a compile error
steps.explain: There is no `$` before the string, so it is ordinary text and the braces mean nothing special. A very common slip.

steps.title: Asking a string about itself
body: A string comes with **members** you reach using a dot.
`word[0]` is the first character. Counting starts at **zero**, so the last character of `"Hello"` is `word[4]`.
> **Tip:** Strings never change. `word.ToUpper()` hands you a *new* string and leaves `word` as it was. To keep the result, store it: `word = word.ToUpper();`

steps.prompt: `string s = "Code";` Match each expression to its value.

steps.explain: `ToUpper()` returned `"DOJO"`, but nothing stored it. The original string is untouched.

steps.title: Fix the receipt
prompt: It compiles, but the output is wrong in three places. Fix it.
hints: Line 6: `3.5` needs to show as `3.50`. A format after a colon does that.
Line 7: the item name should be in capitals. You can call a method inside the braces.

steps.title: Initials
prompt: Using the two variables, print the person's initials with dots, then how many letters the full name has (not counting the space).
It must still work if the names change.
starter: // print the initials, then the letter count
hints: Inside an interpolated string you can write `{first[0]}.{last[0]}.`
